item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00104","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C22","C11","C07"],"selected_candidate_label":"C22","confidence":0.82,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C22 plausibly supplied a material template because both proclamations respond to a recent congressional joint resolution concerning a named, privately organized international industrial gathering, identify its location and dates, and culminate in presidential encouragement or welcome directed toward domestic and foreign participation. The child adapts that machinery from inviting participation in an international trade fair to recognizing a metallurgical congress, welcoming its scientists, and requesting federal cooperation. C11 is structurally similar in its congressional recognition of a named private organization followed by presidential endorsement and a call for support, but it concerns a domestic relief campaign rather than an international technical gathering. C07 shares the congressionally authorized recognition format but is a generic commemorative designation.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Congress of the United States, by joint resolution approved October 10, 1951, has extended its official welcome to the foreign metal scientists who will visit major American production centers and attend the World Metallurgical Congress to be held at Detroit, Michigan, from October 14 to 19, 1951","parent_excerpt":"a joint resolution of the Congress approved on August 12, 1950 ... authorized [the President] to invite ... the States of the Union and foreign nations to participate in the First United States International Trade Fair, to be held at Chicago, Illinois, from August 7 to 20, 1950","explanation":"Both recitals frame a specifically dated and located international industrial event through a congressional joint resolution and emphasize foreign participation."},{"child_excerpt":"do hereby extend recognition to the World Metallurgical Congress ... extend the welcome of this Government to the Congress and to the scientists attending its proceedings","parent_excerpt":"do hereby invite and urge the States of the Union and foreign nations to participate to the fullest practicable extent in the said First United States International Trade Fair","explanation":"The operative clauses perform closely related presidential promotional functions for an international technical or industrial gathering, with the later directive adapting invitation language into recognition and welcome."}]}
